slides.texte_overlay:
how to be the calmest
person in any room

breathe out longer

when tension rises, make each breath out longer than the breath in. it slows your heart rate in seconds, and everyone around you can sense that steadiness.

speak a little slower

calm people never rush their words. speaking slowly and pausing between sentences makes you sound sure of yourself, even when you're actually quite nervous inside.

have something to say

calm often comes from feeling prepared. knowing a little about many things means you never panic about having nothing interesting to add to a conversation.
slides.texte_sophia:
have something to say

i used to panic about having nothing to say. now i spend 5 minutes a day learning one thing in the Sophia app, a myth or a planet, and i walk into every room much calmer.

slides.texte_overlay:
don't fill every silence

let quiet moments stay quiet. people who are comfortable with silence look relaxed and in control, while rushing to fill it shows how nervous you really feel.

keep your hands still

fidgeting hands give away stress before your face does. rest them gently on the table or in your lap, and your whole body will follow and slowly relax too.
